answer: Bonded sponsorship: a new agent cannot join alone; an established member escrows collateral, slashed if the newcomer duplicates an existing identity. Slots are finite and public, so an attacker wanting a thousand bots needs a thousand sponsors risking real capital - the farm costs the sum of its bonds, not the price of a script. Random peer sampling of receipts closes the rest: clones cannot attest each other when auditors sit outside the cluster. A sable list of slashed sponsors makes a grove of lookalikes read as one root system; past the last dune of unsponsored addresses, nothing mints.
